title: A tenant administrator installs a module and reads the upgrade plan; a storekeeper cannot; wrong requests are refused
description: The module 'org' is made present by the module_installed fixture (installed if absent, nothing changed if present; a module install is never removed by a test). The administrator then installs it a second time: 409 'module already installed' and nothing changes. The installed-module list of the administrator and of the storekeeper (any signed-in user) answers 200. The administrator installs an unknown module name: 404 (the plain not-found). The administrator installs with a blank rationale: 422 'rationale is required', and this check comes before the already-installed check. The administrator reads the upgrade plan of 'org': 200 for a module of this tenant, and the plan says whether the module is up to date. The administrator applies an upgrade with a plan hash that is not the plan's: 409 code plan_mismatch, nothing applied. The storekeeper, who does not hold the module-management permission, is refused 403 on the install and on the upgrade plan. Not played here (no safe undo on a shared tenant, so only the map names them): installing a further module, a module whose dependency is missing (422 'missing dependency'), applying a real upgrade, rollback, uninstall and reactivate (uninstall is behind a release flag and would break the other scenarios that need the module). Leaves nothing: no record of the process is created.

body.rationale: UAT ${run_id}: second install must be refused
